paper.citation: Lei, L. and Candes, E. J. (2021). Conformal inference of counterfactuals and individual treatment effects. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B (Statistical Methodology) 83(5), 911-938. DOI: 10.1111/rssb.12445.
paper.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B: Statistical Methodology
paper.source_locator: Section 3.6 'Numerical experiments', arXiv:2006.06138v2 (6 May 2021) PDF p.9 (covariate construction: 'Xj = Phi(X'_j) ... equicorrelated multivariate Gaussian') and PDF p.10 (second and third bullets: 'Y(0) = 0', 'E[Y(1)|X] = f(X1) f(X2), f(x) = 2/(1+exp{-12(x-0.5)})', and 'e(x) = (1/4){1 + beta_{2,4}(x1)}'). The section uses unnumbered bullets, so the locator cites the bullets and page rather than an equation number.

mechanism.name: Lei–Candès (2021) simulation: zero control outcome with a double-sigmoid effect

generation_equations.label: X1-X10
generation_equations.expression: Xj = Phi(X'_j), X' equicorrelated Gaussian with rho = 0, so Xj ~ Uniform(0,1) independently, j = 1..10

sampling.dependence: independent and identically distributed at rho = 0

assumptions: SUTVA: one version of treatment, no interference
Unconfoundedness: the propensity depends on X1 only, and Y(1) depends on X1 and X2, so the assignment is confounded
Overlap: e(X) in [0.25, 0.5] by construction, giving a uniform overlap margin of 0.25
Homoscedastic Gaussian noise with sigma^2 = 1, added only under treatment because Y(0) = 0

properties.notes: Ten ambient covariates, only X1 and X2 active, so effective dimension is 2. The effect is a product across coordinates (interaction) of two logistic sigmoids (nonlinear). d = 10 against the source's sample sizes is not high-dimensional, hence the flag is false.

estimand.name: tau(x0) = E[Y(1) - Y(0) | X = x0]
estimand.definition: Conditional average treatment effect at the declared query points when the control potential outcome is identically zero, so the effect equals the treated conditional mean.

truth.expression: Conditional average treatment effect at the declared query points when the control potential outcome is identically zero, so the effect equals the treated conditional mean.
truth.derivation: Closed form: tau(x0) = f(x1) f(x2) with f a logistic sigmoid, exact up to floating point; cross-checked by a second typing and by the realised outcome column.

adaptations: The source uses d = 10 or d = 100 covariates and an equicorrelation rho in {0, 0.9}; this package fixes d = 10 with rho = 0, so the covariates are independent uniforms and X3..X10 are inert.
Only the homoscedastic scenario sigma^2 = 1 is used; the source also reports sigma^2(x) = -log(x1).
Phi(Z) with Z standard normal is distributed as Uniform(0,1), so the covariates are drawn directly as uniforms; no numerical normal cdf is needed at rho = 0.
The source evaluates interval coverage of CATE and ITE; this package only declares the mechanism and its population CATE. No conformal procedure is run.
